repo.description:
### Summary

The data-import URL fetch helper shared its internal-network exemption with webhooks, so an instance that allowed webhooks to reach local or private addresses also let a user with data-import permission make the server fetch internal URLs and read the responses.

### Details

The outbound request behind the data-import fetch endpoint in `utils.service.ts` attaches request-filtering agents that reject addresses resolving to loopback, link-local, private and other internal ranges. The helper requested those agents under the webhook operation source, and `ssrf.ts` skips filtering for that source when `NC_ALLOW_LOCAL_HOOKS` or `NC_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK` is set, so a setting documented only for webhooks also turned the protection off for data imports. The response body was returned to the caller, making the request non-blind. The fix gives data import its own operation source with a separate opt-in, `NC_ALLOW_LOCAL_DATA_IMPORT`.

### Impact

On an instance with either webhook override set, a user with at least the base Editor role could make the NocoDB server request services on its internal network and read their responses, provided the requested URL path ended in a CSV or spreadsheet extension. Default configurations were not affected.

### Credit

This issue was reported by [@456789TZ](https://github.com/456789TZ).
repo.summary: Server-Side Request Forgery via Data Import URL
